days.title: 1,190 caches, by kind
days.pitch: Every geocache I've found since 2001, one square each, sorted by cache type. Mostly the classic film-canister kind, with a long tail of the odd ones.
days.alt: A waffle chart of 1,190 squares, one per geocache found. Traditional: 996; Virtual: 64; EarthCache: 53; Multi-cache: 39; Mystery cache: 20; Everything else: 18.
days.post_text:
Day 1 of #30DayChartChallenge · Part-to-Whole
1,190 caches, by kind

days.title: Twenty shows
days.pitch: The last twenty concerts in my setlist log, one ticket for each show, grouped by artist.
days.alt: A pictogram of 20 concert tickets, one row per artist: Midnight Oil 3; Coldplay 3; U2 2; Bush 1; The Presidents of the United States of America 1; David Byrne 1; Beastie Boys 1; blink-182 1; Jane’s Addiction 1; Goldfinger 1; Incubus 1; Red Hot Chili Peppers 1; Slayer 1; CAKE 1; Foster the People 1.
days.post_text:
Day 2 of #30DayChartChallenge · Pictogram
Twenty shows

days.title: How the lights stay on
days.pitch: Electricity by source in the countries I've lived in or visited. Each column is a country, as wide as the electricity it makes.
data: Our World in Data, energy data

data_links.name: Our World in Data, energy data

days.alt: A mosaic chart of electricity generation in 2024 for the countries Brooks has visited. The United States is the widest column at 4,391 TWh, then Canada 637, France 562, Germany 496, Indonesia 372, Mexico 355. Each column is split into coal, gas, oil, nuclear, hydro, wind, solar and bioenergy.
days.post_text:
Day 3 of #30DayChartChallenge · Mosaic
How the lights stay on

days.title: Thirty years of carbon
days.pitch: CO₂ per person in 1994, the year I finished at UNR, against 2024, for the places I've lived and traveled.
data: Our World in Data, CO₂ data

data_links.name: Our World in Data, CO₂ data

days.alt: A slope chart of CO₂ per person in 1994 and 2024 for 31 countries. The United States fell from 20.2 to 14.2 tonnes; Luxembourg from 28.6 to 9.7; Indonesia rose from 1.1 to 2.8. The world went from 4.1 to 4.7.
days.post_text:
Day 4 of #30DayChartChallenge · Slope
Thirty years of carbon

days.title: Tree rings
days.pitch: Twenty-five years of geocaching drawn as the rings of a tree: one ring a year, one mark a find, the day of the year going round.
days.alt: Tree rings, one per year from 2001 to 2026, with 1,190 small marks for geocache finds placed by day of year. The busiest year was 2017 with 200 finds.
days.post_text:
Day 5 of #30DayChartChallenge · Experimental
Tree rings

days.title: Room to report
days.pitch: Reporters Without Borders' 2026 press freedom scores for the countries I've visited, against the rest of the world.
days.alt: Dot plot of RSF 2026 press freedom scores for 27 countries Brooks has visited, lowest Ethiopia 34.7, highest Netherlands 88.9; the United States 62.6, rank 64.
days.post_text:
Day 6 of #30DayChartChallenge · RSF Data
Room to report

days.title: Shaken, mostly gently
days.pitch: Washington's earthquakes since 1970, from tremors no one feels to the Nisqually quake. Each step up in magnitude is about ten times rarer.
days.alt: A histogram of 104,043 Washington earthquakes since 1970 on a log scale. Counts peak near magnitude 1 and fall about 8-fold per magnitude step; the largest is the 2001 Nisqually M6.8.
days.post_text:
Day 7 of #30DayChartChallenge · Multiscale
Shaken, mostly gently

days.title: A Lakewood year
days.pitch: A year of daily highs and lows in Lakewood, Washington, wrapped around a clock face of months.
days.alt: A circular chart of 2025 daily temperatures in Lakewood, WA. The hottest day reached 92°F on July 16; the coldest night fell to 22°F on February 12.
days.post_text:
Day 8 of #30DayChartChallenge · Circular
A Lakewood year

days.title: What a house costs
days.pitch: Typical home values in Washington's 39 counties, from Garfield to San Juan, ten years apart.
days.alt: A dumbbell chart of 39 Washington counties' typical home values in 2016 and 2026. San Juan is highest at $897,256, Garfield lowest at $241,396; Pierce County is $559,277.
days.post_text:
Day 9 of #30DayChartChallenge · Wealth
What a house costs

days.title: How long the encore lasts
days.pitch: How many songs each of my concerts ran, by artist. Some bands play a tight hour; some play all night.
days.alt: A dot histogram of 17 concerts by number of songs, from 4 (Presidents of the USA) to 28 (U2); median 19.
days.post_text:
Day 10 of #30DayChartChallenge · Pop Culture
How long the encore lasts

days.title: How high the land stands
days.pitch: The share of land at every elevation in three ranges I love: the Ruby Mountains, Yosemite's Sierra and Mount Rainier.
days.alt: Three violin shapes of land elevation for boxes around the Ruby Mountains, Yosemite's high country and Mount Rainier, with summits marked: Ruby Dome 11,387 ft, Mount Lyell 13,114 ft, Columbia Crest 14,410 ft.
days.post_text:
Day 11 of #30DayChartChallenge · Physical
How high the land stands

days.title: The 81 squares
days.pitch: Every cache I've found on the geocacher's 9×9 grid of difficulty and terrain, drawn in the spirit of Nathan Yau's FlowingData.
days.alt: A 9 by 9 grid of geocache difficulty and terrain ratings with counts; 61 of 81 cells are filled, the most at difficulty 1.5, terrain 1.5 with 282 finds.
days.post_text:
Day 12 of #30DayChartChallenge · FlowingData Theme
The 81 squares

days.title: Who eats whom in Lake Tahoe
days.pitch: Lake Tahoe's food web, from algae to lake trout, including the mysis shrimp and the fish that people brought in.
data: UC Davis Tahoe Environmental Research Center, State of the Lake

data_links.name: UC Davis Tahoe Environmental Research Center, State of the Lake

days.alt: A food-web diagram of Lake Tahoe in four feeding levels, with native species in blue, introduced species in red and the extinct Lahontan cutthroat trout dashed. Lake trout sit at the top; mysis shrimp eat Daphnia and Bosmina.
days.post_text:
Day 13 of #30DayChartChallenge · Ecosystems
Who eats whom in Lake Tahoe

days.title: Trading partners
days.pitch: America's trade in goods in 2024 with the countries I've visited, what it sells against what it buys. A few partners carry most of it.
days.alt: A log-log scatter of US exports versus imports in 2024 for 30 countries. Canada: exports $348B, imports $421B; Mexico $334B and $510B.
days.post_text:
Day 14 of #30DayChartChallenge · Trade
Trading partners

days.title: Higher means snowier
days.pitch: Washington's SNOTEL snow stations: the higher the station, the more water sits in the snow on April 1.
days.alt: A scatter of 69 Washington SNOTEL stations, elevation versus median April 1 snow water equivalent, with fits for west (r 0.65) and east (r 0.32) of the Cascades; overall r 0.36.
days.post_text:
Day 15 of #30DayChartChallenge · Correlation
Higher means snowier

days.title: Why carbon warms
days.pitch: Global temperature against atmospheric CO₂ since 1959. This correlation has a cause: the physics of the greenhouse effect, known since Tyndall and Arrhenius.
days.alt: A scatter of global temperature anomaly against Mauna Loa CO₂ from 1959 to 2025, colored by year, on a log CO₂ axis, falling along a straight line (r 0.96) from 316 ppm to 427 ppm.
days.post_text:
Day 16 of #30DayChartChallenge · Causation
Why carbon warms

days.title: The 2024 bar chart, again
days.pitch: My first chart-challenge try in 2024 was a ggplot remake of an Economist bar chart about lab infections. Here it is again, redone in this year's style.
days.alt: A dot chart of laboratory-acquired infections from 1970 to 2021 by pathogen: Brucella 54, Vaccinia 18, Salmonella 17, Tuberculosis 15, E. coli 11, Ebola 9, Dengue 7, Tularemia 7, Hantavirus 6.
days.post_text:
Day 17 of #30DayChartChallenge · Remake
The 2024 bar chart, again

days.title: Fewer small graves
days.pitch: Under-five mortality against income, 1990 to today, every country an arrow. Almost every arrow points down.
data: Our World in Data, GDP per capita

data_links.name: Our World in Data, GDP per capita

days.alt: Arrows for 178 countries from 1990 to 2024 on log axes of GDP per person and under-five mortality; 99% point down. Ethiopia fell from 202 to 45 deaths per 1,000 births.
days.post_text:
Day 18 of #30DayChartChallenge · UNICEF Data
Fewer small graves

days.title: How America makes its power
days.pitch: Forty years of US electricity, 1985 to 2025, as shares of the whole. Coal's long fall, gas's rise, and wind and solar arriving.
data: Our World in Data, energy data (Ember, Energy Institute)

data_links.name: Our World in Data, energy data (Ember, Energy Institute)

days.alt: A stacked area chart of US electricity shares from 1985 to 2025: coal 58% to 16%, gas 12% to 40%, nuclear about 17%, wind 10% and solar 9% in 2025.
days.post_text:
Day 19 of #30DayChartChallenge · Evolution
How America makes its power

days.title: The shrinking cap
days.pitch: Arctic sea ice at its September low, every year since satellites started watching in 1979.
days.alt: Bars of September Arctic sea-ice extent from 1979 to 2026, falling from about 7.0 to 4.8 million km², with a record low of 3.57 in 2012.
days.post_text:
Day 20 of #30DayChartChallenge · Global Change
The shrinking cap

days.title: Mono Lake, drained and saved
days.pitch: Mono Lake's surface since the 1850s: the fall after Los Angeles started diverting its streams in 1941, and the slow climb since the 1994 decision.
data: Mono Lake Committee lake level data

data_links.name: Mono Lake Committee lake level data

days.alt: A line of Mono Lake's October 1 level from 1850 to 2026: about 6,417 ft in 1941, a low of 6,372.3 ft in 1981, and 6,382.0 ft in 2026, below the 6,392 ft target.
days.post_text:
Day 21 of #30DayChartChallenge · Historical
Mono Lake, drained and saved

days.title: Lakewood's rain, week by week
days.pitch: Ten years of Lakewood rain as a calendar, week by week, made with Altair (Vega-Lite), a tool I hadn't used before.
days.alt: A calendar heatmap of weekly rain in Lakewood, WA, from 2016 to 2025, ten rows of 53 weeks; summers are pale and the late-autumn weeks dark blue. Wettest year 2017, driest 2023.
days.post_text:
Day 22 of #30DayChartChallenge · New Tool
Lakewood's rain, week by week

days.title: Snow at Paradise
days.pitch: Snow depth at Paradise on Mount Rainier, one line for each winter.
days.alt: Lines of daily snow depth at Paradise for 20 winters; the deepest peaked at 228 inches in 2007–2008, the thinnest at 66 in 2014–2015.
days.post_text:
Day 23 of #30DayChartChallenge · Seasons
Snow at Paradise

days.title: Daylight, Lakewood and Hong Kong
days.pitch: Hours of daylight through the year at 47° north and at 22° north, in the bold style of the South China Morning Post's graphics.
days.alt: Two curves of daylight hours through the year: Lakewood from 8.5 to 15.9 hours, Hong Kong from 10.8 to 13.5; they cross near the equinoxes.
days.post_text:
Day 24 of #30DayChartChallenge · SCMP Theme
Daylight, Lakewood and Hong Kong
